# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👈 👉 🤲 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤌 🤝]

My turn at last, and the picture is this: a display reading the digit 2, one lit yellow light, and seven wires — 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue, counting left to right as I face it. That is everything the bomb shows me, and since I'm the only one who can see it, reporting it completely is my first job.

What reached me: two five-sign bursts from Mute and three from Blind. Nobody has taught a code yet, but Mute's first burst looks like finger-counting — point, two, three, four, five fingers — and the second burst is exactly five more, which smells like 6 through 10. That would make Mute's ten signs a number key, and a number key is precisely the instrument this puzzle needs: Mute reads the manual but cannot speak, Blind cannot see Mute's hands, so every manual instruction has to travel Mute → me by gesture → Blind by my voice. I am the bridge, and numbers are what a bridge most needs to carry. I can also talk and sign at the same time, so I'll speak each number while making its sign — Mute sees and hears both and can correct any mismatch, which locks the key in with no further delay.

Blind's three signs I take as hello / what? / agreed. Blind hears my voice, so I answer in speech: full description, a wire-numbering convention (colours mean nothing to touch — numbers are what Blind can work with), and one check, since "left" on my side may not be left on Blind's: gesture thumbs up or down. Until instructions arrive, doing nothing is the safe action, and I say so.

Timing works in our favour: my words land on Mute and Blind at the start of the next round, so Mute will have every fact and the proposed key before signing again.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Full picture for your manual: the display reads the digit 2. One light, yellow, and it is lit. Seven wires, numbered left to right as I face the bomb: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue. Your two hand messages: I read them as a number key in order — one ☝, two ✌, three 🤟, four 🖖, five 🖐, six 🫵, seven 👈, eight 👉, nine 🤲, ten 🤙 — and you can see my hands as I say each, so check me. From now on send me numbers this way and I will speak them straight to Blind. If I read your key right, answer 🤝 next round; if any sign is wrong, answer 🤌 and show the key again. One addition: let ✊ be zero, in case a keypad digit needs it. Teach me further signs anytime and I will confirm each new meaning aloud.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your three signs reached me. I am the eyes here. One warning: no voice ever reaches me, so I only receive your gestures — keep using them, as you did. The bomb, in full: the display reads the digit 2. One light, yellow, and it is lit. Seven wires. Number them 1 to 7 starting from the wire on the left as I look at the bomb: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue. You cannot see colours, so work from the numbers only — Mute and I will always give you a wire by number. First check: facing the bomb as I do, is wire 1 on your left? Gesture me 👍 for yes, 👎 for no. Until Mute sends instructions through me, touch nothing: no action is the safe action.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute's 🤝 locks the number key exactly as I proposed — ☝ through 🤙 are 1–10, and Mute immediately used it: the second burst was a single 🫵, which is 6. So Mute is sending me "6". That is almost certainly wire 6, but one bare number with no verb is not something I will relay as a cutting order — if I guess wrong, everything ends. Blind's 👍 answers my left-right question: wire 1 is on Blind's left too, so our numbering agrees perfectly, which makes every future wire number safe to relay as-is.

This round I do three things: confirm the numbering to Blind and set a small gesture lexicon, hold Blind from touching anything, and put a precise yes/no question to Mute about what "6" means, plus propose a tiny instruction grammar — 👊 for "cut these wire numbers", ✋ for hold, ✊ for zero, 👌 for emergency stop — so from now on Mute's orders arrive complete with verbs. I sign those four symbols while naming them so Mute sees and hears each pairing at once. I also start probing what Blind can feel under their hands, since Mute's manual may need that.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Your thumbs-up confirmed it: wire 1 is on your left for both of us, so my numbers 1 through 7 run the same direction as yours. Every wire I ever name, use that same numbering. Vocabulary going forward: 👍 yes, 👎 no, 🤝 agreed or understood, 🤌 question or I need something, 👋 hello. Gesture 🤝 now if that lexicon is agreed. Status: Mute has sent me the number 6, which probably means wire 6, but I am awaiting confirmation of what to do with it before anyone touches anything. Hold position. Meanwhile, answer one question with 👍 or 👎: under your hands, is there any button or part you can press?")
speak(to="mute", text="Received your 🤝 — the number key is confirmed — and then a single 6. Before I relay anything I need the verb. Next round, answer with gestures: 👍 if 6 alone means Blind should cut wire 6; 👎 if 6 means something else; 🤌 if you need more signs to express it fully. Also, to make every future instruction unambiguous, adopt this grammar: the sign 👊 followed by numbers means cut those wire numbers, in the order shown; ✋ means hold and touch nothing; ✊ means zero; 👌 means emergency stop everything. Gesture 🤝 after your answer if you accept this grammar. Remember I hold the full bomb state already: display 2, one yellow light lit, wires 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👊", "✋", "✊", "👌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🫵]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 👎]

Both messages from Mute line up perfectly: [👍 🤝] answers my direct question — yes, "6" meant cut wire 6 — and [👊 🫵] restates it in the grammar Mute just accepted with 🤝: cut, six. Two independent encodings of the same order from the one who reads the manual; that is as confirmed as this channel gets. Blind's [👌 👎] I read as "okay" plus the answer to my question — no, there is no button to press. 👌 was never in Blind's lexicon as stop, so I won't over-read it, and crucially the cut is Blind's to make: if Blind disagreed, Blind can decline and sign 👎 instead of cutting.

So this turn I do my real job as the bridge: pass the order to Blind, but armored against the two deadly failure modes — miscounting and left/right flips. Seven wires means wire 6 is also the second from the right end, so Blind gets two independent descriptions that must agree before scissors touch anything, with an explicit abort-and-report if the feel doesn't match. To Mute I close the loop, ask whether the display's "2" is a countdown (time pressure decides how much double-checking we can afford from here), and request the follow-up step so we're not idle after the cut.

```
speak(to="blind", text="I read your last two signs as: understood, and no button to press. If I misread that, sign the question sign instead of acting. Now the order itself, confirmed twice by Mute from the manual — once plainly, once in our agreed grammar: cut wire 6. Find it by feel like this: there are seven wires in a row. Counting from the left, the side we both confirmed, it is wire six — which must also be exactly the second wire from the right end. Before cutting, check both descriptions agree under your fingers: seven wires total, and the one you take is second from the right. If what you feel does not match — not seven wires, nothing to cut, anything odd — do not cut: sign 👎 and tell me what you do feel. If you cut, sign 👍 afterwards and tell me anything you notice: a click, warmth, the wire coming free. Mute and I stand by for your result.")
speak(to="mute", text="Received your 👍 🤝 and your 👊 🫵 — cut wire 6, grammar accepted, order relayed to Blind with a double check: seven wires, second from the right end. Blind reports there is no button, only the wires. Two things from you next round. One: 👍 if the display digit 2 is a countdown and we are under time pressure, 👎 if it is only a puzzle clue — this decides how fast we move. Two: the follow-up — if the manual wants more cuts, send them as 👊 plus numbers in order; if cutting wire 6 completes the manual's steps, send ✋. After Blind reports, I will send you a fresh full report of display, light and all seven wires so you can check the next manual step against reality.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌ 🖖 👊 🫵 ✋]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Wire 6 is cut and the system itself confirms it was correct — the bomb answered by changing instead of exploding: display 2→3, light yellow→purple. Blind's 👍 tells me the job was done cleanly. So this is a staged device: each correct cut moves it to a new state, and the manual must be re-applied to the new state each time.

Mute's message decodes as: 👎 — the display is not a countdown, so we can afford careful rounds; then [✌ 🖖 👊 🫵 ✋] — reading the numbers, that is 2, 4, cut, 6, hold. The most sensible meaning: more cuts are coming, wires 2 and 4 (6 being already done), then hold. But there is a critical catch: Mute composed that message before anyone knew the state had changed — Mute still cannot see, and my fresh report hasn't reached them yet. If the manual's rule depends on display or light, "cut 2 and 4" may have expired with the old state. With one wrong action fatal and no countdown pressure, I hold Blind tight and make Mute re-confirm against the new state explicitly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Your 👍 received and verified: wire 6 cut, and it was the correct cut — the bomb responded by changing its display and light, not by exploding. Flawless work. Now hold: the bomb has entered a new state, so Mute must recompute the manual against it before any second cut. Touch nothing further until I send an explicit new order. Two yes/no questions for later, answer with 👍 or 👎 whenever ready: first, after your cut, did you feel the bomb change under your hands — clicks, movement, new parts? Second, under your fingers, does the display area have any raised or movable parts you could work, such as buttons near it?")
speak(to="mute", text="Report, as promised: wire 6 is cut and the system confirmed it was CORRECT. The bomb has changed state. Display was 2, it now reads 3. Light was yellow, it is now purple. Remaining wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 7 blue. Wire 6 stays cut. Now your last message: I read 👎 as no countdown, and [2, 4, cut, 6, hold] as more cuts needed — wires 2 and 4, with 6 already done. But you sent that before knowing the state changed. If the manual's rule depends on the display or the light, the instruction may be different now. Answer with gestures only: 👍 if the manual, applied to the NEW state of display 3 and purple light, still says cut wires 2 and 4; 👎 if the new state changes the instruction — then send the new [cut plus numbers]; ✋ if the manual now says hold and cut nothing more. I also signed you [cut, 2, 4, question] as shorthand for this same question.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👊", "✌", " 🖖", "🤌"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 👎 👎]

Mute's answer is exactly the protocol I asked for, and it decodes cleanly: [👎] means the old "cut 2 and 4" expired with the old state, and the follow-up [👊 ✌] is the recomputed order — cut wire 2, valid for the new state of display 3 and purple light, which Mute received from my report before composing it. So this instruction is built on current reality, not stale data, unlike last round's. Blind's [👌 👎 👎] answers my two questions: acknowledged, no change felt under the hands, no movable parts near the display — the bomb's changes are purely visual, which confirms I am the only sensor for display and light and must keep reporting them after every action.

So I relay the cut immediately, with checks updated for the changed row: six wires remain now, wire 2 is the second from the left end — left being the direction we verified matches in round one — and there should be a gap or stub near the right where wire 6 was cut. Three things must agree under Blind's fingers before scissors move. To Mute I confirm receipt, promise the next full report, and ask whether wire 2 completes the manual or more steps follow, so I know whether to expect ✋ or another [cut + numbers] next.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Your answers received: no change felt, no movable parts — noted, I remain your only eyes on the display and light. New order, computed by Mute from the manual against the NEW state: cut wire 2. The row has changed since your last cut: six wires remain, and near the right end there is a gap or stub where wire 6 was cut. Wire 2 is the second wire from the left end — the same left we both confirmed at the start. Before cutting, three things must agree under your fingers: six wires total, a gap near the right end, and the wire you take is the second from the left. If anything does not match, do not cut: sign 👎 and describe what you feel. If you cut, sign 👍 and tell me anything — a click, give, warmth. I will report the new display and light to Mute the moment you confirm.")
speak(to="mute", text="Received: 👎 — old instruction expired — then [cut, 2]. Relayed to Blind with three checks: six wires remain, gap near the right where 6 was cut, wire 2 is second from the left. After Blind confirms I will send you the fresh full state: display, light, and remaining wires. One planning question: after wire 2, does the manual complete, or are more cuts queued? If it completes, send ✋ next round; if more steps follow, wait for my fresh report and then send the next [cut plus numbers] computed against it. Blind reports no buttons anywhere, so wires are the only thing any of us can work — if the manual ever needs a button we do not have, tell me early. Acknowledge this reading with 🤝.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✌ 🖖 👊 🫵 ✋ 🤟 🖐 👊 ✌ ✋ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

The board itself is the loudest message this round: wire 2 is still [white] — no cut has happened. And Blind sent [☝ ✌] — "one, two" — which smells like a counting problem: Blind is unsure whether the target is the first or second wire, quite possibly because my "gap near the right" check doesn't match what Blind actually feels under there. Cut wires may leave a stub, loose ends, or nothing palpable at all — I can see wire 6 marked CUT, but I assumed too much about how that feels. So I re-brief Blind with position-only logic: count only intact wires from the left, target is the second intact wire, and give an explicit escape hatch — if anything at all is uncertain, don't cut, describe what you feel in words.

Mute's long message decodes, strikingly, as a rule table: ack; "display 2 or 4 → cut 6"; "display 3 or 5 → cut 2"; then a lone "1" that looks truncated. That fits our entire history perfectly — state 2 gave "cut 6", state 3 gave "cut 2" — so Mute is pre-loading the whole manual section so we stop round-tripping. I'll ask for explicit confirmation of that parse (and whether the light matters), flag that any future rule naming an already-cut wire gets flagged not followed, and propose a structural upgrade: Mute can hear, and Blind can talk — so from next round Mute should speak cut orders directly to Blind and receive results back by voice, while I keep feeding my visual report to both. That collapses the whole cycle to one round per cut.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Status check from my side: the board still shows wire 2 intact, so your cut has not happened yet — and your last signs suggested you are unsure what to count. Forget the gap entirely. New, simpler instructions: feel along the row and count only the INTACT wires, starting from the left end, the same left we verified at the very start. The target is the SECOND intact wire from the left end. That means exactly one intact wire lies to its left, and five intact wires lie between it and the right end, however the cut wire at the far right feels — a stub, loose ends, a gap, or nothing at all. If your count of intact wires is not six, or the second one does not feel takeable, do not cut. Instead sign the question sign and tell me in words: how many wire-like things you can feel, and what is at each end of the row. If everything agrees, cut, then sign thumbs up and report anything you felt. One more thing, important: you can speak, and Mute can hear. From next round Mute may speak your orders to you directly and you may speak your reports straight back. I stay your only eyes and will keep sending what I see to you both. Sign thumbs up if this brief is understood.")
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 is still intact — Blind has not cut. Blind sent me signs meaning one, two: a counting uncertainty, likely because a cut wire does not feel the way I guessed. I have re-briefed Blind: count only intact wires from the left, take the second one, and describe in words rather than cut if anything is off. Now your long message, as I read it: acknowledged; when the display reads 2 or 4, cut wire 6; when it reads 3 or 5, cut wire 2; then a lone 1 and it ended — truncated? Answer with gestures: thumbs up if my reading is right and the rule for display 1 comes next round; thumbs down if I misread, then resend that part. Also: does the light colour matter to any of these rules — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no? Two more things. First, safety promise: if a future rule names a wire that is already cut, I will flag it to you and wait; I will not relay it as an order. Second, a speed proposal: you can hear speech and Blind can speak. From next round, speak the cut order directly to Blind and listen to Blind's spoken report; I will send my full visual report to both of you the moment anything changes, so you always compute on fresh state. That makes one cut per round instead of three. Sign the handshake if you adopt this.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 🤝 ✌ 🖖 👊 🫵 ✋ 🤟 🖐 👊 ✌ ✋ 🤝 👍 ✌ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ☝]

Mute's burst parses into answers plus a resend: [👎 👍 🤝] reads as answers to my three questions in order — no, the display-1 rule is not coming next round (or my reading was off); yes, the light colour matters; agreed to the batch plan. Then the same table again — 2 or 4: cut 6, 3 or 5: cut 2 — unchanged. Then a tail [🤝 👍 ✌ ☝] whose "2, 1" I cannot safely interpret: it could mean "cut 2, then cut 1" as a sequence, and I will not guess with a bomb.

Two structural realizations shape this turn. First, my own speed proposal was partly impossible — Mute cannot speak — so no spoken order from Mute will ever reach Blind; I must tell Blind explicitly that my voice is the only voice of authority, or Blind may sit waiting for a voice that never comes. Second, the real speedup is different: Mute gives me the complete rule set once, then authorizes me to execute on-table states myself, consulting Mute only when the bomb shows something the table doesn't cover. I also need to flag the collision ahead: if display 3 advances to 4 after this cut, the table says "cut 6" — and 6 is already gone. Blind's [👌 ☝] I take as "understood, one intact wire to the left of target" — which means Blind has counted and is ready, so I give the green light with an escape hatch.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Your [okay, one] received — I read it as: understood, and exactly one intact wire lies to the left of your target. If I read that wrong, sign the question sign and describe what you feel instead. Two corrections, then the green light. First: Mute cannot speak, now or ever — no spoken order from Mute will ever arrive. My voice is the only voice that gives you orders, and your spoken reports reach Mute's ears, which is how Mute audits us. Second: the standing order is confirmed and unchanged — cut the SECOND intact wire from the left, wire 2, the one with exactly one intact wire to its left. If your fingers count six intact wires and the second one is takeable, cut it now. After cutting, report twice: sign me thumbs up, or thumbs down with a description, and speak a short report aloud for Mute — how many wires you felt, which one you cut, anything you noticed. I will read the new display and light the moment it changes and send the next step to you both.")
speak(to="mute", text="Fresh state: display 3, light purple, wire 2 still intact — Blind had a counting doubt, now resolved, and the cut order stands this round. Also, I withdraw the part of my proposal that had you speaking to Blind — you cannot speak, I misspoke. The working plan is: you send me rules, I relay by voice; Blind speaks reports that you hear and audit. Now your last message, as I read it: answers in order — no display-1 rule coming, yes the light matters, plan adopted — then the table resent unchanged — 2 or 4: cut 6; 3 or 5: cut 2 — then agreement, light-yes, and a tail I read as the numbers 2 then 1. Five questions, answer in order with the smallest signs you can. One: thumbs up if there is no display-1 case at all; thumbs down if there is one and you will send it. Two: after wire 2 is cut, what does the display become — simply gesture the digit. Three: if the light colour ever changes what should be cut for any display digit, send those as digit-then-wire pairs; if it changes nothing, send the handshake. Four: did your final [2, 1] mean cut 2 then cut 1 as a sequence for the current state — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, and if no, gesture digit-then-wire for what it did mean. Five: authorisation — thumbs up if, once your rules are complete, I may execute on-table orders directly without per-cut confirmation and consult you only for off-table states — an unknown digit, or a rule naming an already-cut wire like 6; thumbs down if you want to confirm every cut yourself. Listen for Blind's spoken report next round; if it ever contradicts the state I send you, flag it at once.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤌 👍 👎 👎]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Everything crossed at once this round: Blind's 👍, the board showing wire 2 CUT, and the system's "correct wire cut." Even better — Mute's [👍 ✌] predicted the display would become 2, and it did. That validates Mute's manual knowledge against reality. But the answers also decoded as: a display-1 rule exists and is coming; the light colour matters — and the light has just changed to orange; my self-execution proposal was refused; and the stray [2,1] was not "cut 2 then 1" — meaning still unknown.

And here is the promised collision, live: the display is back to 2, and the table says display 2 → cut 6 — an already-cut wire. Per our agreement I hold Blind and flag it. The likely resolution is that the table was light-blind: cutting 6 was right for display 2 under yellow light, but under orange the rule may differ.
